keyVerseText: Joseph of Arimathaea, an honourable counsellor, which also waited for the kingdom of God, came, and went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.
rootMeaning: The Greek adjective εὐσχήμων (euschḗmōn) derives from the combination of εὖ (eû), meaning 'good' or 'well,' and σχῆμα (schēma), meaning 'form' or 'figure.' Literally, it conveys the idea of one who is 'well-formed' or possessing a good outward appearance. This root sense extends beyond mere physical comeliness to include qualities of grace, dignity, and decorum, suggesting an elegance of bearing and a noble demeanor that reflects inner virtue as well as outward honor.
usageInScripture: The term εὐσχήμων appears five times in the New Testament, where it is translated variously as 'honourable,' 'an honourable,' 'of honourable,' and 'comely.' This range of translation highlights the word's dual emphasis on both physical appearance and moral character. It is used to describe individuals of noble rank or respectable demeanor, as well as to signify behavior that is seemly and becoming. Such consistency in usage underscores the word's association with dignity and respectability in both social and ethical contexts.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding εὐσχήμων enriches our grasp of biblical character and conduct by emphasizing that true honor and nobility are not merely external but deeply connected to moral integrity and grace. The word's root meaning reminds believers that God values a life well-formed in character—one that exhibits decorum and dignity reflective of His holiness. This aligns with the Christian call to live honorably before God and man, embodying the noble qualities of Christ. Recognizing this term's significance encourages believers to pursue a faith that is both inwardly genuine and outwardly respectable, honoring God through conduct that is both graceful and upright.
keyVerseReflection: In Mark 15:43, Joseph of Arimathaea is described as 'an honourable counsellor,' a translation of εὐσχήμων, which highlights his respected status and noble character. This word adds depth to the verse by portraying Joseph not only as a man of social standing but also as one whose demeanor and integrity enabled him to act boldly in requesting Jesus’ body. His honorable nature serves as a model of faithful courage and reverence for Christ, demonstrating how dignity and grace empower believers to serve God courageously even in difficult circumstances.
